item.title: Leavitt Says She’ll Return to MAGA Inc. After White House
item.description: White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt said she will return to MAGA Inc., the president’s super political action committee, when she leaves her post later this month.
item.dc:creator: Hadriana Lowenkron

item.title: Seigle: Squeezing Iran Means Confronting China
item.description: Senior Nonresident Scholar at the Center for Strategic and International Studies Clayton Seigle says a successful US economic pressure campaign against Iran would require confronting China, a major buyer of Iranian energy, potentially putting Washington's "fragile trade war détente" with Beijing at risk. Seigle says tougher pressure could also push energy prices higher if Iran retaliates against shipping or regional infrastructure, with US gasoline prices an important political concern ahead of the midterms. He speaks with Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg's 'Balance of Power.' (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: 'Hopeful' US. Canada Will Reach Deal: Fmr. Trade Official
item.description: Former Canadian Trade Minister Mary Ng says she is hopeful the US and Canada can reach a trade agreement before Friday's deadline, pointing to positive signals from negotiators on both sides. Ng also says Canada should continue diversifying its trade relationships, pointing to opportunities across Asia including Japan, South Korea, Singapore and Indonesia. She speaks with Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg's 'Balance of Power.' (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US and Canada Race to Beat Tariff Deadline With Metals a Focus
item.description: US and Canadian negotiators haggled over the scope of tariffs on metal imports from Canada as they raced to beat a midnight deadline to seal a trade deal that would avert 50% levies on billions of dollars of goods, people familiar with the matter said.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer A. Dlouhy, Josh Wingrove and Joe Deaux

item.title: Trump Says It Was Bessent’s Choice to Intervene in Bond Market
item.description: President Donald Trump said he did not direct Scott Bessent to intervene in the bond market this week, saying that the Treasury secretary acted on his own authority.
item.dc:creator: Hadriana Lowenkron

item.title: Trump to 'Isolate' Iran, US Treasuries Whiplash | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 8/21/2026
item.description: White House Correspondent Jeff Mason explains President Trump's vow to isolate Iran's economy as he plans to travel to South Carolina to campaign for the midterms. Bloomberg Intelligence Chief US Interest Rate Strategist Ira Jersey and Alpine Saxon Woods Chief Market Strategist Sarah Hunt break down the week of whiplash for US Treasury yields. Then, ITG's Chris Mecray discusses how the digital infrastructure services company has been doing post-IPO for this week's edition of CFO Briefing. Plus, Bloomberg News Legal Analyst June Grasso breaks down Supreme Court Chief Justice John Roberts' decision to allow Trump to keep building the White House Ballroom. Finally, Bloomberg News Senior Legal Reporter Ava Benny-Morrison dives into her report that the DOJ sought Egan-Jones' records to probe Mark Walter's business. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Crypto Rules Are Coming Even If Clarity Act Fails
item.description: There’s a lot regulators can do while the landmark bill languishes.
item.dc:creator: Nathan R Dean

item.title: Trump Eases Tariffs on Ground Beef | Radio Balance of Power: Early Edition 8/21/2026
item.description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondent Kailey Leinz discusses the latest from the Trump Administration. On today's show, former Deputy US Trade Representative Sarah Bianchi, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Brownstein Hyatt Farber Schreck Partner Sarah Mercer and former US National Security Advisor John Bolton. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Administration Dismisses a Dozen Officials From Fannie Mae
item.description: The Trump administration dismissed a dozen senior staff from mortgage giant Fannie Mae this week, according to an official familiar with the matter, the latest move in a push to remake the lender.
item.dc:creator: Josh Wingrove

item.title: Trump Says Controversial US Attorney Ed Martin to Leave Role
item.description: President Donald Trump said Ed Martin, a senior Justice Department official, was leaving his post in the administration, the latest in a series of high-profile departures ahead of November’s midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Josh Wingrove

item.title: Permanent Tariffs on Canada Hurt the US, Freeland Says
item.description: Former Canadian Deputy Prime Minister Chrystia Freeland, talks about the importance of Canada reaching a trade deal with the US. She says putting permanent tariffs on Canadian steel and aluminum will hurt the US, especially car manufacturers in Detroit. She speaks on Bloomberg Television’s Wall Street Week With David Westin, to which she is a regular contributor. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Chief Justice Lets Trump Keep Building Ballroom for Now
item.description: US Chief Justice John Roberts said President Donald Trump can keep building his massive new White House ballroom for now, giving the Supreme Court more time to consider a longer-term order allowing continued construction.
item.dc:creator: Greg Stohr

item.title: Trade Deal to Leave ‘Bad Outcome’ for Canada and US, Ex-Minister Says
item.description: Mark Carney is doing what no previous Canadian leader has done by accepting that President Donald Trump can impose tariffs despite the terms of the North American trade pact, the country’s former deputy prime minister said.
item.dc:creator: Melissa Shin

item.title: Piracy Observer Says Somali Incidents Rising as Navies Stretched
item.description: The world’s top maritime piracy observer said incidents off the coast of Somalia are on the rise again after a pair of fresh attacks this week — as two major regional conflicts stretch naval forces in the area thin.
item.dc:creator: Charles Gorrivan

item.title: Lula Calls Trump to Seek Talks Over US Tariffs on Brazil
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva urged Donald Trump to resume negotiations over US tariffs on Brazil during a Friday phone call, seeking to soothe relations with Washington ahead of the country’s October election.
item.dc:creator: Simone Iglesias

item.title: Iran’s President Says Better to End War Today
item.description:
Iran’s president urged an end to the war with the US, in his latest pushback against hardliners who want to continue the conflict.
“It would be better to end the war today, when we have power and dignity, and with the whole world acknowledging our victory,” Masoud Pezeshkian said, according to the semi-official Iranian Students’ News Agency.
Pezeshkian, along with Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and lead negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, have been vocal advocates of ending the war through diplomacy and prioritizing economic recovery since the signing of a now-collapsed ceasefire. His comments come as the conflict shows no sign of a quick resolution and US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is expected to unveil plans to economically isolate Iran and its trading partners. We get the latest from Bloomberg's Tyler Kendall in Washington. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: MBS, Macron to Sign Bilateral Deals, Address Energy Routes
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron and Saudi Arabian Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman are set to oversee the signing of bilateral deals and discuss alternative routes to the disrupted Strait of Hormuz during talks on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Nayla Razzouk

item.title: Germany Says Weapons Cache Points to Hybrid Attack Plans
item.description: Germany’s top security official confirmed the discovery of a cache of weapons on the outskirts of Berlin and said authorities are investigating the possible involvement of foreign security agents in a range of planned attacks.
item.dc:creator: Michael Nienaber

item.title: Trump Tariff Relief on Ground Beef Sparks Backlash from Ranchers
item.description: President Donald Trump said he would allow tariff relief for some ground beef imports in a bid to lower prices for American consumers, a key concern ahead of November midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Mason and Ilena Peng

item.title: How Germany Lost Its Industrial Edge
item.description: Fierce competition from China and high energy costs are just two of the reasons Germany’s famous industrial machine has stalled. How did this crisis come to pass, and can Germany adapt in time? (Corrected to replace image of German currency at 1:17) (Source: Bloomberg)
